correctness.rationale: The exact initial-color-cohort reduction proves that capped group sizes 0,1,2 preserve the threshold-two predicate on each shore, and absent cohorts are masked from both excitation counts and state equality. There are exactly (3^3-1)^2=676 signatures. The attached certificate enumerates all, yielding least periods 1,3,4, T<=5 and the complete signature histogram. The first-recurrence profiles of the occupied cohorts equal those of the underlying labelled configurations. Only one recurrent period-three signature and two period-four signatures occur, proving the exact orbit counts via multinomial enumeration. The size-feasibility criterion, stabilized for sizes >=6, verifies the sharp maximum-entry table for all shore sizes. Exact EGF coefficient extraction counts all initial configurations without omission or duplication. Standalone code regenerated the entire certificate and independently compared 73449 direct labelled initial conditions; finite direct experiments corroborate but are not substituted for the cohort reduction.

originality.rationale: The reviewed 1991/1993 threshold-range paper addresses spatial lattice excitation and supplies the model, not an exact complete-bipartite classification. The 2016 finite-graph structural theorem uses excitation threshold one; the 2021 threshold-two work studies infinite regular trees. The closest accessible earlier biclique theorem uses threshold one and yields period three when both shores have full three-color support (at least one vertex of each color), unlike the present two-per-color condition; its primitive-four orbit count also differs. The older threshold-two crown-graph theorem has the matched-edge-deleted graph and additional periods, not this graph. Actual published-record, source and parameter searches revealed no statement implying the period onset 4/6, complete period counts and sharp five-step bound together. This is a qualified best-knowledge conclusion, not a universal uniqueness guarantee.

value.rationale: The two-neighbor excitation condition is a historically motivated control parameter in excitable media, not an arbitrary slice. The theorem resolves an exact dynamic invariant for all complete bipartite graphs: distinct sharp 4/6 vertex thresholds for onset of four- versus three-cycles, exact primitive orbit counts, an all-configuration first-entry census, and a globally sharp five-update transient ceiling. The phase change from rare four-cycles to dominant immediate three-cycles as shore sizes grow gives a mathematically motivated finite-size and probabilistic distinction. This is a natural complete classification with a uniform 676-signature reduction, not a known-table recomputation.
